messages:
maya: Heads-up — canary rollout for the kernel-selection change (switching to aggressive prefetch policy) triggered OOMs on several long-ctx workers around 11:42. I paused the rollout. :warning:
teja: Ugh, ok. How many OOMs and on which models? any repro commands?
maya: ~6 OOMs across 3 hosts, all with gptx-long-256 / seq=1024 workload. Quick paste of the node logs: ```
[11:42:13] mem_total=63.8GB mem_used=61.2GB kv_live=29.1GB kv_frag=12.4GB worker=worker-17 OOM
[11:42:14] thread=tokgen slot=3 kernel=new-prefetch aggressive=true
```
sam: Can we bisect to the kernel-selection commit? which commit flipped the prefetch knob?
maya: The toggle landed in commit abc1234 -> enabled aggressive prefetch by default for kernel selector. I rolled back the canary group, which stopped further OOMs.
jordan: I ran a quick perf capture on a repro host. Flamegraph shows a big spike in KV memcpy during warmup; appears duplicate pinning of the same KV page across two paths after the new kernel handoff. Link: https://perf/reports/3170001234/flame (private)
teja: Can you dump the KV histograms before/after the switch? I want to see live_bytes, pinned_pages, and eviction_pressure buckets. Use: `perf record --kv-histogram` and `rd-report kv_hist.json`
maya: Pasted a trimmed histogram snapshot: ```
pre-switch: kv_live_bytes=28.7G pinned_pages=812 eviction_pressure=0.12
post-switch: kv_live_bytes=45.3G pinned_pages=1404 eviction_pressure=0.78
```
sam: That delta is huge. Sounds like warmup duplication — prefetch may be requesting overlapping slices which bypass the usual coalescing, causing duplicate allocations. @jordan can you confirm if the kernel path uses a separate allocation cache?
jordan: Confirmed. New kernel path keeps a local prefetch buffer that wasn't deduping against the KV slab map during the handoff. Patch idea: check slab map before allocating and fallback to shared pin when page already present. I'll sketch a fix.
ci-bot: [perf/regression] CI perf tests detected a 22% increase in peak RSS on long-ctx job (matrix: runtime/kernel-selection) after abc1234 on branch main. https://ci/reports/3170001234
teja: For immediate mitigation we should: 1) halt rollout (done), 2) add a guard to avoid double-pinning, or 3) revert abc1234 if we can't patch quickly. Preference for guard + hotfix.
maya: Agree. I filed a rollout-hold and added the canary rollback note in the release thread.
sam: If @jordan can produce a small PR with a guard and a unit test reproducing double-pin, we can fast-track a revert-if-needed plan. I'll prepare a revert PR but won't merge unless we fail the hotfix.
jordan: Will open PR with test and a soft-fallback to shared pin. Also adding telemetry to emit `kv_double_pin_count` metric.
teja: Once PR is up, let's run the reproduce command I used locally: `./dev/serve --model gptx-long --kernel new-prefetch --seq 1024 --workload replay/longtrace.json` and monitor kv_double_pin_count + rss.
maya: Thanks all. Leaving notes in the incident doc. If anyone finds extra repro hosts, ping me. :eyes:
